set.approach: From the Glacier Gorge parking area, follow the trail to Black Lake, then carry on around to the lake's east side and climb the drainage that leads toward Spearhead. The slabs sit above the southeast corner of the lake and the drainage brings you to their base. They are wide, so the line is your choice, and when the slabs have not formed they are hard to pick out from below. Check the avalanche forecast before heading in.
set.descent_text: The simplest way down is to reverse the climb through the snow, with a few short, low-exposure ice downclimbs. Climbing past the end of the ice and descending the gully beside Spearhead is also possible, but it adds a long stretch of deep snow.

review.notes: Route page: approach and both descent options. Single source.

set.approach: Take the trail from the Glacier Gorge parking area to Black Lake. The flow is the left-most, easiest-looking ice visible from the lake, on the east-facing wall between the lake and Stoneman Pass. It begins as a broad, low-angle slab. The approach is long, and skis help on the way out when there is enough snow. Slopes below the climb can be loaded with snow. Check the avalanche forecast before heading in.
set.descent_text: After the second pitch you can traverse right into a bowl and descend it, but that bowl is prone to slab avalanches. The quickest way off from higher up is to traverse north into the steep bowl below Arrowhead Peak, which is dangerous when avalanche hazard is high. A longer and safer option is to head south across to the flats under Spearhead, then drop to the lake where the summer trail meets it.

review.notes: Route page: position, approach character, three descent options. Single source.

set.approach: The ice is on the south side of Glacier Gorge, only a few minutes east of Reflections. It is hard to see from directly below but shows up well from farther west up the gorge. It forms as two short curtains with a snowy ledge between them.

review.notes: Route page location text. No descent stated, so none written.

set.approach: The flows spill over the left-hand ridge along the final approach to Black Lake, so they are visible from the trail. The broad slab on the left is easy, and the more interesting variations form to its right. A near-vertical curtain about 30 feet wide gives the best start.
set.descent_text: From the top, downclimb to the right on ledges to reach a tree with rappel slings. All three variations finish at the same anchor point.

review.notes: Route page: location and descent. Single source.

set.approach: Stoneman is the big flow directly right of West Gully, above Black Lake. Take the Glacier Gorge trail to the lake and look up at the back wall. Check the avalanche forecast before heading in.
set.descent_text: Walk off to the right (east). Rappelling toward climber's right is exposed to avalanche danger.

review.notes: Route page: location and walk-off. Single source.

set.approach: The ice forms at the top of a deep gully to the left of West Gully and right of Black Lake Slabs. It can be seen from Black Lake, which you reach by the trail from the Glacier Gorge parking area. Check the avalanche forecast before heading in.

review.notes: Route page location only; no descent stated.

set.approach: The route lies just right of Stoneman, at the back of the Black Lake cirque. The Glacier Gorge trail leads to the lake below. Check the avalanche forecast before heading in.
set.descent_text: The usual way off is to walk east. If avalanche danger looks bad, descend on V-threads instead.

review.notes: Route page location and descent options. Single source; the page itself is unsure which flow carries the name.

set.approach: Start from George's Corner, the tight hairpin on the Pikes Peak Highway, and head south up the drainage. At the clearing or pit, cut across the hillside to the right (west) until you reach the toe of Abruzzi Ridge. The easiest way on is at the climber's right, with harder variations farther left. Check the avalanche forecast before heading in.
set.descent_text: Walk off to the east by way of Big Blue.

review.notes: Route page: start and descent. Single source.

set.approach: Park at the switchback on the Pikes Peak Highway near Glen Cove and walk into the north-face cirque above it. The Three Little Pigs couloirs, also called the Flying W, lie along the cirque's left (east) side, and you hike to their foot. The center couloir is the middle of the three. Check the avalanche forecast before heading in.

review.notes: Route page: approach only; descent not stated.

set.approach: Park near Glen Cove on the Pikes Peak Highway and hike to the couloir system that forms a W shape when all three lines are in. The W is to the left of Little Italy, and this route is the right-most of the three couloirs. Check the avalanche forecast before heading in.

review.notes: Route page location; descent not stated.

set.approach: Park at George's Corner, the tight left hairpin on the Pikes Peak Highway, and go south up the old drainage as far as a big pit. Then slant rightward across the slope and the climb appears between Little Italy on one side and The Cornice Bowl on the other. Check the avalanche forecast before heading in.

review.notes: Route page location; descent not stated.

set.approach: Follow the county road toward Quandary's Blue Lakes and park at the fork below the lower lake. The ice forms in the gully left of the Golden Goat Buttress, which sits directly above that fork. The approach is short. The flow comes into shape only briefly after a freeze and thaw cycle, so check avalanche conditions.
set.descent_text: Scramble off to the west from the rock outcrops at the top of the second pitch, then work west and pick a gully that goes down.

review.notes: Goat Urea page gives gully position, parking and descent; buttress page agrees on parking and a west-side descent.

set.approach: From Piney Lake near Vail, follow the valley until the trees begin. The road to the lake is closed to vehicles in winter and spring, so the lake itself takes a tour, hike or snowmobile ride. The trail then fades, and unmaintained terrain with steep boulders leads to the couloir below Knee Knocker Saddle. Go up it to the saddle. The line begins in a narrow couloir immediately east of the saddle. Check the avalanche forecast before heading in.
set.descent_text: Go down the CC Rider Couloir on the south side of the summit. Skis or snowshoes are very useful for the long exit down the Piney valley.

review.notes: Route page: approach and descent; summit top-out stated. Single source.

set.approach: The ice is in Whitewater Creek where the drainage drops over the west side of Grand Mesa. After the winter road closure the Lands End road becomes a very long ski or snowmobile trip from Highway 65, while earlier in the season a shorter walk is possible. Parties rappel in from the top of the flow.

review.notes: Route page: location and access. Descent not stated.

set.approach: The flow hangs at the spot where Coal Creek spills off the rim of Grand Mesa, a few miles from Lands End toward Highway 65. Before the Lands End road closes, a four-wheel-drive vehicle can reach a point close to the rim; later in the season the approach is a long ski or snowmobile trip from Highway 65. Parties rappel in from the rim, so the climb is entered from above.

review.notes: Route page: location and access. Descent not stated.

set.approach: Leave the road end in Watson Creek and scramble up the creekbed until huge boulders block the way, then walk around them or, when the slot on the right wall holds good ice, squeeze up through that. Keep following the creek: a short slot of ice comes next, and the main pillars start farther up the drainage. Deep snow, if any, makes the upper approach slow. The climb is a series of separate pillars with walking between them.
set.descent_text: Reverse the route pillar by pillar. Rappel the pillars from trees, boulders, chockstones or the belay arch, or from V-threads in the ice if you trust it. The big pillars take two ropes. Where the creek ice lies back, downclimb it, and walk around the lowest boulder-blocked step.

review.notes: Route page: approach and rappel descent; counts of raps omitted. Single source.

co_hallett_south_side_cracklin_otis_bran.skip_reason: No page found for this route; could not place it.

set.approach: From the Half Moon Pass trail, either continue down to the Cross Creek drainage and head up it to Lake Patricia, or, to avoid the talus, contour left near treeline to the cliffs above the lake and rappel in from a tree. The ice is on the northwest-facing buttress at the south end of the lake, and the huge flow is easy to recognise. Check the avalanche forecast before heading in. Dismas takes the broken right-facing corner on the left side of the main flow.
set.descent_text: Rappel from V-threads at the top. Reaching the ground in one rappel needs double ropes.

review.notes: Route page: approach and rappel descent. Single source.

set.approach: From the Half Moon Pass trail, either continue down to the Cross Creek drainage and head up it to Lake Patricia, or, to avoid the talus, contour left near treeline to the cliffs above the lake and rappel in from a tree. The ice is on the northwest-facing buttress at the south end of the lake, and the huge flow is easy to recognise. Check the avalanche forecast before heading in. Gestas takes the thin sheet on the sweeping rock face right of the main flow.

review.notes: Gestas page refers to Dismas for location; descent from Dismas page covers both.

co_idaho_springs_water_wheel_reverse_phy.skip_reason: Page says the route is not legal to climb and gives no approach or descent; nothing to write.

set.approach: Start from James Peak Lake in the east basin and go around it to the northwest side. Climb a moderately steep snowfield over talus to the upper basin below the east face. Sky Pilot, Super Star and Shooting Star all rise from the same wide snowfield. Pass Sky Pilot first, which bends away at a lower angle. Higher up, Super Star branches off steeply. Shooting Star is the other narrow couloir. Rockfall can reach the wide lower couloir in early season, and the east face softens early in the day. Check the avalanche forecast before heading in.
set.descent_text: From the summit, walk northeast down a gentle scree slope past the top of Super Star (look over the cornice from a rock point). Continue east until a gentler slope appears that is good for glissading, then return to the lake's northwest shore.

review.notes: Route page: approach and descent. Single source.

set.approach: Hike to the talus beneath James Peak's east face. The route follows the lowest, longest ridge that runs out of the talus, to the left of Shooting Star and Sky Pilot, beginning at a pale rock band that sits a little above the flat bench. From the talus you can see the crux dihedral partway up. In a snowy cirque the start can be hard to pick out. The wall sheds rock in thaw conditions.

review.notes: Route page: start location. Descent not stated.

set.approach: Begin up Sky Pilot Couloir and look right for an easy ramp of high fourth to low fifth class. Scramble up about 50 feet and the chimney crack is obvious above. It links Sky Pilot to Shooting Star near the middle of each, and serves as a start for Shooting Star when rockfall is active at the couloir's entrance.

review.notes: Route page: location. Descent not stated.

co_link_ups_and_rodeos_pike_s_peak_alpin.skip_reason: No page found for this route; could not place it.

set.approach: The Little Cimarron road is plowed only a short way in winter, and the usual starting point is a pullout at a sharp left bend. Driving farther depends on conditions, so the route can be a very long walk up the road. The ice cannot be seen from the road. Once you find the right drainage, hike east a short way up into an amphitheater to reach the ice on the right.

review.notes: Route page: access and walk-in. Descent not stated.

set.approach: Starting at the switchback just south of the Little Cimarron trailhead, follow the Uncompahgre Trail, number 246, until the drainage coming off Sheep Mountain's north face crosses it, near 10,200 feet. Leave the trail and walk west up that drainage, easiest on the south side until you must cross, to a hidden amphitheater. The pillar stays out of sight until you are nearly on it. Avalanches from Sheep's north face can funnel down this canyon. Check the avalanche forecast before heading in.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the small tree at the top of the second pitch, walk back down to the first pitch and rappel from a rock pinch beneath the large chockstone. Walking off the whole climb is also possible by leaving the canyon to the north above the second pitch and then dropping east, though that is probably not quicker.

review.notes: Route page: approach and descent. Single source.

set.approach: From the Little Cimarron trailhead, follow the trail until ice shows in the side drainage to the east, a short way beyond the approach to Perky Turkey. Go down to the creek, then climb the slope beside it. The cliff is short and broad, with several flows.

review.notes: Route page: location. Descent not stated.

set.approach: Beginning at the switchback just below the Little Cimarron trailhead, walk the Uncompahgre Trail (#246) to the signed junction for the Little Cimarron Trail, shortly after the creek crossing. The climb is directly above, but the easier way is to stay on the main trail heading south to an unsigned fork with the High Mesa Trail, number 133. Turn right and follow it northwest to a prominent drainage, then walk up the drainage to the ice.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the trees with cord above the runnel. A single long rope may not reach the ground, in which case make a second rappel from a tree on the ledge.

review.notes: Route page: approach and rappel descent. Single source.
